To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

there is a high degree of population structure between island and mainland populations of southern elephant seals, and that there are differences between the two populations in morphology and in genetic diversity at both mtDNA and nuclear DNA markers.

(1) southern elephant seals from the South Georgia island rookery are genetically and morphometrically distinct from seals from the mainland rookery at Valdes Peninsula; (2) mtDNA control region sequences from the South Georgia population are distinct from those of the mainland population and from sequences from other island rookeries; (3) mtDNA sequences from the mainland population are distinct from sequences from the other island rookery; (4) the mainland population has low mtDNA sequence diversity

the mainland population of southern elephant seals is likely to have been founded by only a small number of females, and that there are differences between the two populations in morphology, which may be due to differences in the selective environments experienced by the two populations.
